theory.intro: A **piecewise-defined function** uses a different rule on each part of its domain. To find $f(c)$, decide which domain condition contains $c$, then substitute into that rule only.
facts: A piecewise function joins two or more **subfunctions**, each used on its own part of the domain.
To evaluate $f(c)$, find the domain condition containing $x = c$ and substitute into that rule only.
At a boundary $x = a$, $\le$ or $\ge$ includes the boundary, while $<$ or $>$ excludes it.
On a graph, a filled circle ($\bullet$) means the endpoint is included and an open circle ($\circ$) means it is excluded.
Each $x$ in the domain has exactly one output, so a graph cannot have two distinct included outputs at the same $x$-value. Coincident included endpoints represent the same output.
For an expression like $f(-2) + f(3)$, work out each value from its own branch, then do the arithmetic.
steps: Identify which domain condition contains the input value $x = c$
Substitute $x = c$ into the corresponding subfunction rule
Evaluate the expression to calculate the value of $f(c)$

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Since $-2<1$, use the first rule.
$\begin{aligned}f(-2)&=\dfrac{15}{-2+5}\\&=\dfrac{15}{3}\\&=5\end{aligned}$

(b) The condition $x\ge1$ includes the boundary $x=1$.
$\begin{aligned}f(1)&=2(1)+3\\&=5\end{aligned}$

(a) Since $1<3$, use $2^{x}$.
$h(1)=2^{1}=2$

(b) Since $3\le3\le5$, use the constant rule.
$h(3)=6$

(c) Since $7>5$, use $(x-3)^{2}$.
$\begin{aligned}h(7)&=(7-3)^{2}\\&=4^{2}\\&=16\end{aligned}$

(a) At $x=1$, the filled circle at $(1,4)$ is included. The open circle at $(1,1)$ is excluded.
$g(1)=4$

(b) At $x=-1$, the graph passes through $(-1,3)$, so $g(-1)=3$.
$\begin{aligned}g(-1)+g(1)&=3+4\\&=7\end{aligned}$

(a) Since $1.5>0$, use $x^{2}-1$.
$\begin{aligned}p(1.5)&=(1.5)^{2}-1\\&=2.25-1\\&=1.25\end{aligned}$
Since $-0.5\le0$, use $5-2x$.
$\begin{aligned}p(-0.5)&=5-2(-0.5)\\&=6\end{aligned}$
Subtract the function values.
$\begin{aligned}p(1.5)-p(-0.5)&=1.25-6\\&=-4.75\end{aligned}$

(b) The condition $x\le0$ includes $x=0$, while $2>0$ uses the second rule.
$\begin{aligned}p(0)&=5-2(0)\\&=5\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}p(2)&=2^{2}-1\\&=3\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}2p(0)+p(2)&=2(5)+3\\&=13\end{aligned}$

foundation.question_text: Given the piecewise function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x - 2, & x < 2 \\ x^{2} + 1, & x \ge 2 \end{cases}$, evaluate $f(4)$.
For the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 5, & x \le 1 \\ 8 - x^{2}, & x > 1 \end{cases}$, evaluate $f(-3)$.
For the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 5, & x \le 1 \\ 8 - x^{2}, & x > 1 \end{cases}$, evaluate $f(1)$.
For the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 5, & x \le 1 \\ 8 - x^{2}, & x > 1 \end{cases}$, evaluate $f(3)$.

A piecewise function is defined as $g(x) = \begin{cases} -2x, & x < -1 \\ 3, & -1 \le x \le 4 \\ x - 1, & x > 4 \end{cases}$.
Evaluate $g(2)$.
foundation.solution_text:
Since $2$ lies in the interval $-1 \le x \le 4$, the constant subfunction applies:
$g(2) = 3$

Look at $x = 0$ on the vertical axis.
The open circle at $(0,4)$ indicates $x = 0$ is not included in that branch.
The filled dot is at $(0,2)$, which includes $x = 0$.
$f(0) = 2$

At $x = 2$, check the endpoint markers.
The open circle at $(2,1)$ excludes that point.
The filled dot at $(2,4)$ includes that point.
$h(2) = 4$

development.question_text: For the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} x + 4, & x < 0 \\ 4 - x^{2}, & 0 \le x < 3 \\ 2x - 11, & x \ge 3 \end{cases}$, evaluate $f(-2)$ and $f(3)$.
Given $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3 - x, & x \le 2 \\ 2x - 1, & x > 2 \end{cases}$, evaluate the expression $f(-1) + f(4)$.
development.solution_text:
Evaluate each function value:
$f(-1) = 3 - (-1) = 4$
$f(4) = 2(4) - 1 = 7$
Add the results:
$f(-1) + f(4) = 4 + 7$
$= 11$

development.question_text: Given $g(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2} - 3, & x < 1 \\ 4 - x, & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$, evaluate $3g(-2) - 2g(1)$.
development.solution_text:
Evaluate $g(-2)$ using $x^{2} - 3$ (since $-2 < 1$):
$g(-2) = (-2)^{2} - 3 = 4 - 3 = 1$
Evaluate $g(1)$ using $4 - x$ (since $1 \ge 1$):
$g(1) = 4 - 1 = 3$
Substitute into the expression:
$3g(-2) - 2g(1) = 3(1) - 2(3)$
$= 3 - 6$
$= -3$

Read $f(-1)$ from the filled dot at $(-1,0)$:
$f(-1) = 0$
Read $f(2)$ from the filled dot at $(2,3)$:
$f(2) = 3$
Sum the values:
$f(-1) + f(2) = 0 + 3$
$= 3$

development.question_text:
Let $h(x) = \begin{cases} 2^{x}, & x < 2 \\ 5 - x, & 2 \le x \le 5 \\ (x - 4)^{2}, & x > 5 \end{cases}$.
Find the values of $h(0)$, $h(2)$, and $h(6)$.

A mobile plan charges according to the piecewise function $C(t) = \begin{cases} 20, & 0 \le t \le 100 \\ 20 + 0.15(t - 100), & t > 100 \end{cases}$, where $C(t)$ is cost in dollars for $t$ minutes.
Determine the cost for $240\text{ minutes}$ of usage.

Let $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{12}{x+4}, & x < 2,\ x \ne -4 \\ 3x - 4, & x \ge 2 \end{cases}$.
Evaluate $f(-1)$ and $f(2)$.

mastery.question_text: Given $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x + 2, & x < 1 \\ 7 - x^{2}, & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$, evaluate $f(3) - f(-4)$.
Given $g(x) = \begin{cases} 6 - 3x, & x \le 0 \\ x^{2} - 2, & x > 0 \end{cases}$, evaluate $g(2.5) - g(-1.5)$.

A function is defined by $f(x) = \begin{cases} 4 - x, & x < -1 \\ x^{2} - 3, & -1 \le x \le 3 \\ 2x - 5, & x > 3 \end{cases}$.
Evaluate $f(-3.5) - f(2.5)$.
